questions.stem: A person who repairs and services motor vehicles is called a
questions.explanation: A motor mechanic diagnoses faults and repairs and services cars and other vehicles.

questions.stem: The professional who installs and repairs electrical wiring in buildings is an
questions.explanation: Electricians install wiring, sockets, switches and fittings and repair electrical faults.

questions.stem: The professional who estimates the quantities and cost of materials needed for a building project is a
questions.explanation: A quantity surveyor prepares bills of quantities and cost estimates for construction work.

questions.stem: A person who produces technical drawings of objects and buildings is called a
questions.explanation: Draughtsmen prepare accurate technical drawings used by engineers and builders.

questions.stem: Technology can be described as the
options: application of scientific knowledge to solve practical problems
questions.explanation: Technology uses scientific knowledge to make tools, machines and processes that solve problems.

questions.stem: Which of the following shows an importance of technology in agriculture?
options: Technology stops farmers from selling produce
Farmers must work only with their hands
Tractors and irrigation pumps increase food production
questions.explanation: Machines and modern methods make farm work faster and increase yields.

questions.stem: At night, pedestrians should wear bright or reflective clothing so that
options: they can see in the dark
questions.explanation: Light-coloured and reflective clothing makes pedestrians visible to drivers in poor light.

questions.stem: On a road without a footpath, pedestrians should walk
options: with their backs to the traffic
in the middle of the road
questions.explanation: Facing the traffic lets pedestrians see approaching vehicles and step aside in time.

questions.topic: Safety guidelines for cyclists and motorcyclists
questions.stem: For safety, cyclists should
options: ride side by side across the road
keep close to the edge of the road and use hand signals
carry heavy loads on the handlebar
questions.explanation: Keeping to the edge and signalling clearly let other road users know what the cyclist will do.

questions.topic: Safety guidelines for cyclists and motorcyclists
questions.stem: A commercial motorcyclist should NOT
options: switch on the headlamp at night
questions.explanation: Overloading a motorcycle makes it unstable and hard to control, which causes crashes.

questions.stem: Before overtaking another vehicle, a motorist should
options: sound the horn and overtake at a bend
make sure the road ahead is clear and give the correct signal
questions.explanation: Overtaking is safe only when the driver can see that the road ahead is clear and has warned other road users.

questions.stem: The Nigerian agency responsible for road safety and traffic control on highways is the
questions.explanation: The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) enforces traffic rules and promotes road safety.

questions.stem: Drinking alcohol before driving is dangerous mainly because it
options: slows the driver's reaction time and judgement
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the brain, so the driver reacts slowly and makes poor decisions.

questions.stem: Using a blunt chisel is dangerous mainly because
options: it is too light to hold
more force is needed and the tool may slip
questions.explanation: A blunt tool needs extra force, which makes slipping and injury more likely.

questions.stem: Touching a machine with faulty wiring can cause
questions.explanation: Faulty insulation lets current flow through the body, causing electric shock.

questions.stem: A fire extinguisher in the workshop is used to
questions.explanation: Fire extinguishers are safety devices for putting out fires before they spread.

questions.stem: Safety boots with steel toecaps protect the
questions.explanation: Steel toecaps prevent injury if heavy tools or materials fall on the feet.

questions.stem: Wearing an overall or apron in the workshop protects the
questions.explanation: An overall covers the body and clothes from dirt, oil and sparks.

questions.stem: A bucket of sand is kept in the workshop mainly for
options: putting out small fires and soaking up oil spills
questions.explanation: Sand smothers small fires and absorbs spilled oil, reducing slipping.

questions.stem: Which is a workshop safety rule?
options: Play with tools during practical lessons
Report every accident, however small, to the teacher
questions.explanation: Reporting accidents ensures injuries are treated and the cause is corrected.

questions.stem: A fire caused by an electrical fault should NOT be put out with
options: a fire blanket after switching off the power
questions.explanation: Water conducts electricity and can electrocute the person; the power should be switched off and a suitable extinguisher used.

questions.stem: One main aim of first aid is to
options: punish the person who caused the accident
replace the work of doctors completely
preserve life and stop the condition from getting worse
questions.explanation: First aid keeps the casualty alive and stable until medical help takes over.

questions.stem: A minor burn from touching hot metal should first be
options: cooled under cool running water for about ten minutes
questions.explanation: Cool water reduces heat in the skin, eases pain and limits damage.

questions.stem: A suspected broken arm should be
options: kept still with a splint or sling before going to hospital
questions.explanation: Immobilising the limb prevents further damage and pain.

questions.stem: A small metal particle gets into a student's eye during filing. The first aider should
options: rub the eye hard to remove the particle
rinse the eye gently with clean water and not let the student rub it
remove the particle with a sharp needle
cover the eye and continue working
questions.explanation: Rubbing or using sharp objects can scratch the eye; gentle rinsing may wash out the particle, and the student should then see a health worker.

questions.stem: To check a casualty's circulation, a first aider should
options: count the number of breaths only
feel for a pulse at the wrist or neck
check the colour of the shoes
questions.explanation: A pulse shows that the heart is pumping blood round the body.

questions.stem: The national emergency telephone number in Nigeria that can be dialled free from any phone is
questions.explanation: 112 connects callers to emergency services such as police, fire and ambulance.

questions.stem: Moving victims from a dangerous place to safety or to hospital is called
questions.explanation: Evacuation is the removal of people from danger to a safe place or for medical care.

questions.stem: The federal agency that coordinates rescue and relief during disasters such as floods in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: The National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) coordinates disaster response and relief.

questions.topic: Securing the environment, vehicle and victims
questions.stem: At a crash scene, the vehicle is made safe by
options: switching off the engine and applying the handbrake
questions.explanation: Switching off reduces the risk of fire and the handbrake stops the vehicle from moving.

questions.topic: Securing the environment, vehicle and victims
questions.stem: A crash victim who may have a neck or spine injury should
options: be made to sit up at once
not be moved unless there is immediate danger such as fire
be carried on a motorcycle to hospital
be pulled out quickly by the arms
questions.explanation: Moving a person with a spinal injury can cause paralysis, so they are kept still until trained help arrives unless their life is in danger.

questions.stem: Obeche is easily identified as a wood that is
options: light in weight and pale (cream) in colour
questions.explanation: Obeche is a light, pale wood that is easy to work.

questions.stem: Mahogany is a wood that is
options: black and used for charcoal only
white and used for paper only
yellow and used for roofing sheets
reddish-brown and used for good furniture
questions.explanation: Mahogany is a reddish-brown hardwood valued for furniture and panelling.

questions.stem: The property of a metal that allows it to be hammered into different shapes without breaking is
questions.explanation: Malleable metals can be beaten into sheets and shapes.

questions.stem: Which of the following metals rusts easily?
questions.explanation: Mild steel contains iron, which rusts in air and moisture; aluminium, copper and gold do not rust.

questions.stem: The property of a metal that allows it to be drawn into wires is
questions.explanation: Ductile metals such as copper can be stretched into thin wires.

questions.stem: The shiny appearance of a freshly cut metal surface is called
questions.explanation: Lustre is the shine that metals have when clean.

questions.stem: Ceramic tiles are used on walls behind cookers mainly because they
options: resist heat and are easy to clean
questions.explanation: Ceramics withstand high temperatures and have smooth, washable surfaces.

questions.stem: Roofing sheets are commonly made from
questions.explanation: Metal roofing sheets are light, strong and keep out rain.

questions.stem: Thatch made from grass and leaves is used in traditional buildings mainly for
questions.explanation: Grass and leaves are bundled as thatch to cover roofs.

questions.stem: PVC pipes are used in buildings mainly for
questions.explanation: PVC pipes are light, do not rust and carry water and waste.

questions.stem: Glass is used for windows mainly because it
questions.explanation: Glass is transparent, so it lets light into rooms while keeping out rain and wind.

questions.stem: Granite chippings (gravel) are added to concrete mainly to
questions.explanation: Coarse aggregate makes concrete strong and reduces the amount of cement needed.

questions.stem: Steel rods are placed inside concrete beams and columns mainly to
options: help the concrete resist bending and tension
questions.explanation: Concrete is strong in compression but weak in tension; steel reinforcement carries the tension.

questions.stem: Wood is commonly used for making
options: furniture such as tables and chairs
questions.explanation: Wood is strong, easy to work and attractive, so it is used for furniture.

questions.stem: Plastic is used for chairs and buckets mainly because it is
questions.explanation: Plastic products are light, waterproof, durable and cheap.

questions.stem: Aluminium is used for cooking pots mainly because it
options: is light, conducts heat well and does not rust
questions.explanation: Aluminium heats food quickly, is easy to handle and resists corrosion.

questions.stem: Rubber is used for shoe soles mainly because it is
questions.explanation: Rubber bends, absorbs shock and provides grip.

questions.stem: Brass is used for taps and door handles mainly because it
questions.explanation: Brass, an alloy of copper and zinc, does not rust and keeps a bright, golden appearance.

questions.stem: In air seasoning, timber is stacked in an open-sided shed with small strips of wood called stickers between the boards in order to
options: allow air to circulate round each board
questions.explanation: Stickers leave gaps for air flow, so the timber dries evenly.

questions.stem: The age of a tree can be estimated by counting its
questions.explanation: A tree usually adds one growth ring each year, so the number of rings shows its age.

questions.stem: Good, well-seasoned timber is used for making
questions.explanation: Strong, seasoned timber is used for structural work, doors and furniture.

questions.stem: A board that curves along its length on its face, like a bow, has the defect called
questions.explanation: Bowing is a curve along the length of the wide face of a board.

questions.stem: A board that curves across its width so that it looks like a shallow trough has the defect called
questions.explanation: Cupping is a curve across the width, usually caused by uneven drying.

questions.stem: A board whose ends turn in opposite directions so that it is no longer flat has the defect called
questions.explanation: Twist is a spiral distortion along the length of the board.

questions.stem: Forcing preservative deep into timber inside a closed cylinder under high pressure is called
questions.explanation: Pressure treatment drives preservative deep into the wood, giving long-lasting protection.

questions.stem: Applying preservative to timber by soaking it in a tank of preservative for some time is called
questions.explanation: Steeping lets the preservative soak into the surface layers of the timber.

questions.stem: Extracting metal from its ore by heating it in a furnace is called
questions.explanation: Smelting uses heat and chemical reactions to separate the metal from its ore.

questions.stem: Shaping hot metal by hammering or pressing it is called
questions.explanation: Blacksmiths forge metal by heating it and hammering it into shape.

questions.stem: Passing hot or cold metal between heavy rollers to make sheets and plates is called
questions.explanation: Rolling reduces the thickness of metal to produce sheets, plates and bars.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of metal processing methods
questions.stem: A disadvantage of sand casting is that the castings may
options: contain blowholes and have a rough surface finish
questions.explanation: Gas trapped in the mould can leave holes, and the sand leaves a rough surface that may need machining.

questions.stem: Stainless steel is used for making spoons and cutlery mainly because it
questions.explanation: Stainless steel contains chromium, which prevents rusting.

questions.stem: Soft solder is an alloy of
questions.explanation: Soft solder melts at a low temperature and is made from tin and lead.

questions.stem: Duralumin is used in making aircraft bodies mainly because it is
questions.explanation: Duralumin, an aluminium alloy, combines low weight with high strength.

questions.topic: Methods of processing clay, ceramics and glass
questions.stem: Making a pot by building up long rolls of clay one on top of another is called
questions.explanation: In the coil method, rolls of clay are joined layer by layer and smoothed.

questions.topic: Methods of processing clay, ceramics and glass
questions.stem: Shaping molten glass by blowing air into it through a long pipe is called
questions.explanation: Glass blowers inflate molten glass to form bottles and vases.

questions.topic: Methods of processing clay, ceramics and glass
questions.stem: Before clay is used for pottery, it is kneaded (wedged) mainly to
options: remove air bubbles and make it even
questions.explanation: Trapped air can make pots crack or burst during firing, so the clay is wedged.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of clay, ceramic and glass processing methods
questions.stem: An advantage of glass as a material is that it
questions.explanation: Waste glass can be melted down and made into new glass products.

questions.topic: Production and uses of clay, ceramics and glass
questions.stem: Bricks are made by moulding clay into shape and then
questions.explanation: Firing hardens the clay so the bricks become strong and durable.

questions.topic: Examples of plastic and rubber products
questions.stem: Which of the following is a rubber product?
questions.explanation: Rubber bands are made from stretchy rubber.

questions.topic: Methods of processing plastics and rubber
questions.stem: Making plastic pipes by forcing molten plastic through a shaped opening (die) is called
questions.explanation: Extrusion pushes material through a die to form long shapes such as pipes and rods.

questions.topic: Methods of processing plastics and rubber
questions.stem: Plastic bottles are usually made by
questions.explanation: In blow moulding, air is blown into a softened plastic tube inside a mould to form a hollow bottle.

questions.topic: Methods of processing plastics and rubber
questions.stem: Heating raw rubber with sulphur to make it stronger and more elastic is called
questions.explanation: Vulcanisation links rubber molecules, making the rubber hard-wearing, as used for tyres.

questions.stem: Thermosetting plastics are used for saucepan handles mainly because they
questions.explanation: Once set, thermosetting plastics cannot be softened by heat, so they stay firm on hot pans.

questions.topic: Examples of drawing instruments and materials
questions.stem: The instrument used to draw circles and arcs is the
questions.explanation: A pair of compasses holds a pencil lead at a fixed distance from a point, drawing circles and arcs.

questions.topic: Examples of drawing instruments and materials
questions.stem: The instrument used to draw irregular curves that cannot be drawn with compasses is the
questions.explanation: French curves have many curved edges for drawing smooth irregular curves.

questions.topic: Uses of drawing instruments and materials
questions.stem: A protractor is used to
questions.explanation: A protractor is marked in degrees for measuring and drawing angles.

questions.topic: Uses of drawing instruments and materials
questions.stem: Which pencil grade is commonly used for lettering and darkening outlines?
questions.explanation: HB is softer than H grades and gives a darker line, suitable for lettering and outlines.

questions.stem: A tee-square should not be used as a cutting edge or for hammering because
options: it will turn into a set square
its edge may be damaged and lose its straightness
questions.explanation: A damaged blade edge no longer draws true straight lines.

questions.topic: Care of drawing instruments and materials
questions.stem: An erasing shield is used to
options: protect nearby lines while a small part of a drawing is erased
questions.explanation: The shield has holes that expose only the part to be erased.

questions.stem: Border lines are drawn on drawing paper mainly to
options: frame the area in which the drawing is done
questions.explanation: The border marks the drawing area and gives a neat finish.

questions.stem: The title block on a drawing sheet is usually placed at the
questions.explanation: The bottom right corner is the standard position, where it can be seen easily when sheets are filed.

questions.stem: Which information is usually written in the title block?
options: Only the price of the paper
Title of the drawing, scale, name and date
questions.explanation: The title block identifies the drawing and the person who made it.

questions.stem: Faint guidelines are drawn before freehand lettering in order to
options: keep the letters of uniform height
questions.explanation: Guidelines keep letters even and aligned.

questions.stem: A pencil sharpened to a chisel (knife) edge is best for
questions.explanation: A chisel edge stays sharp longer along a straightedge and gives lines of even thickness.

questions.stem: Using the 45 degree and 30/60 degree set squares together on a tee-square, which of the following angles can be drawn?
questions.explanation: 75 degrees = 45 + 30; combinations of the two set squares give multiples of 15 degrees.

questions.stem: The basic materials needed for freehand sketching are
options: a tee-square and drawing board only
a pencil, an eraser and paper
questions.explanation: Freehand sketching is done without instruments, using only pencil, eraser and paper.

questions.stem: Freehand sketching is useful mainly because it
options: is a quick way of recording ideas
questions.explanation: Sketches let designers put down and communicate ideas quickly.

questions.stem: When sketching a long straight line freehand, it helps to
options: look only at the pencil tip
draw it in one very fast stroke without looking
keep the eye on the end point of the line
questions.explanation: Watching where the line is going keeps it straight.

questions.stem: To sketch an irregular shape freehand, it is helpful to first draw
options: light guide lines or an enclosing box
questions.explanation: Light guides help to get the proportions right before the outline is darkened.

questions.stem: The distance all round a circle is called the
questions.explanation: The circumference is the boundary line of a circle.

questions.stem: A quarter of a circle is called a
questions.explanation: A quadrant is bounded by two radii at right angles and a quarter of the circumference.

questions.stem: The part of a circle bounded by two radii and an arc is a
questions.explanation: A sector looks like a slice of cake.

questions.stem: Using the tee-square and the 30/60 degree set square, a circle can be divided into
questions.explanation: Lines at 0, 30, 60 and 90 degrees through the centre divide the circle into 30-degree parts, giving 12.

questions.stem: A normal to a circle at a point on the circumference always
options: touches the circle at two points
passes through the centre of the circle
is perpendicular to the radius at that point
questions.explanation: The normal is the line along the radius through the point, so it passes through the centre.

questions.stem: A triangle with all three sides of different lengths is called
questions.explanation: In a scalene triangle no two sides or angles are equal.

questions.stem: A triangle with two equal sides is called
questions.explanation: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides and two equal base angles.

questions.stem: A right-angled triangle has its two shorter sides measuring 30 mm and 40 mm. What is the length of the longest side?
questions.explanation: By Pythagoras, the hypotenuse = square root of (30 x 30 + 40 x 40) = square root of 2,500 = 50 mm.

questions.stem: The centre of the circle that passes through all three corners of a triangle (circumscribed circle) is found where the
options: perpendicular bisectors of the sides meet
questions.explanation: The circumcentre is equidistant from all three vertices, which is where the perpendicular bisectors of the sides cross.

questions.stem: A polygon with five sides is called a
questions.explanation: Penta means five.

questions.stem: A polygon with seven sides is called a
questions.explanation: Hepta means seven.

questions.stem: A polygon whose sides and angles are not all equal is called
questions.explanation: A regular polygon has all sides and angles equal; otherwise it is irregular.

questions.stem: What is the size of each exterior angle of a regular pentagon?
questions.explanation: The exterior angles of any polygon add up to 360 degrees, so each is 360 / 5 = 72 degrees.

questions.stem: What is the size of each interior angle of a regular octagon?
questions.explanation: Each exterior angle = 360 / 8 = 45 degrees, so each interior angle = 180 - 45 = 135 degrees.

questions.stem: Plane figures are shapes that have
questions.explanation: Plane figures such as squares and triangles are flat, two-dimensional shapes.

questions.stem: Which plane figure has four equal sides and four right angles?
questions.explanation: A square has four equal sides and four right angles.

questions.stem: A four-sided figure with all sides equal but no right angles is a
questions.explanation: A rhombus has equal sides, but its angles are not 90 degrees.

questions.stem: What is the area of a triangle with a base of 60 mm and a height of 40 mm?
questions.explanation: Area = ½ x base x height = ½ x 60 x 40 = 1,200 square millimetres.

questions.stem: A square is to have the same area as a rectangle measuring 90 mm by 40 mm. What is the length of the side of the square?
questions.explanation: Area of rectangle = 3,600 square millimetres; side of square = square root of 3,600 = 60 mm.

questions.topic: Enlargement and reduction of plane figures
questions.stem: A rectangle measuring 80 mm by 60 mm is reduced in the ratio 1:2. What are the new dimensions?
questions.explanation: Each side is halved: 80 / 2 = 40 mm and 60 / 2 = 30 mm.

questions.topic: Enlargement and reduction of plane figures
questions.stem: In the radial line method of enlargement, lines are drawn
options: from a fixed point through each corner of the figure
questions.explanation: Lines from the centre of enlargement through each vertex are extended in the given ratio to locate the new corners.

questions.stem: In an isometric drawing of a cube, how many faces of the cube can be seen?
questions.explanation: An isometric view shows the top and two side faces together.

questions.stem: Isometric grid paper helps a student to
options: draw isometric lines quickly and accurately
questions.explanation: The grid already has lines at 30 degrees and vertical lines to follow.

questions.topic: Isometric drawing of simple shape blocks
questions.stem: In an isometric drawing, the three isometric axes are spaced at
questions.explanation: One axis is vertical and the other two are at 30 degrees to the horizontal, so the angles between them are 120 degrees.

questions.topic: Isometric drawing of simple shape blocks
questions.stem: In an isometric drawing of a rectangular block, the vertical edges of the block are drawn
questions.explanation: Vertical edges of the object remain vertical in isometric drawing.

questions.topic: Isometric drawing of simple shape blocks
questions.stem: In isometric drawing, measurements along the isometric axes are usually drawn
questions.explanation: Isometric drawing uses true lengths along the three axes.

questions.stem: In cavalier oblique drawing, the receding lines are drawn
options: at one quarter of their length
questions.explanation: Cavalier oblique uses full depth, while cabinet oblique uses half depth.

questions.stem: Besides 45 degrees, the receding lines in an oblique drawing may also be drawn at
questions.explanation: Oblique receding lines are commonly at 45 degrees, but 30 or 60 degrees may also be used.

questions.stem: A box 60 mm deep is drawn in cabinet oblique. What length is drawn along the receding axis?
questions.explanation: Cabinet oblique uses half the true depth: 60 / 2 = 30 mm.

questions.stem: In oblique drawing, the face of an object with circles or the most detail should be placed
options: at the front, facing the viewer
questions.explanation: The front face is drawn in its true shape, so circles there appear as true circles and are easy to draw.

questions.stem: The view of an object seen from the front is called the
questions.explanation: In orthographic projection the front view is called the front elevation.

questions.stem: The view of an object seen from the side is called the
questions.explanation: The end elevation shows the object as seen from the left or right side.

questions.stem: The two principal planes used in orthographic projection are the
options: vertical plane and the horizontal plane
questions.explanation: Views are projected onto the vertical plane (elevations) and the horizontal plane (plan).

questions.stem: The projection symbol drawn in the title block, showing two views of a truncated cone, is used to indicate
options: whether first angle or third angle projection has been used
questions.explanation: The arrangement of the cone views in the symbol tells the reader which angle of projection was used.

questions.topic: Placing principal views in the quadrants
questions.stem: In first angle projection, the end view seen from the left of the object is placed
options: to the right of the front elevation
to the left of the front elevation
questions.explanation: In first angle, each view is placed on the side opposite to where it is viewed from, so the left view goes to the right.

questions.stem: Hidden edges of an object are shown in an orthographic drawing by
questions.explanation: Hidden detail lines are thin, short dashes.

questions.stem: Centre lines on a drawing are shown as
options: thin chain lines (long and short dashes)
questions.explanation: Centre lines are thin chain lines used for axes of symmetry and centres of circles.

questions.stem: In dimensioning, the arrowheads of a dimension line should
options: stop far from the projection lines
questions.explanation: Arrowheads should just touch the projection (extension) lines to show the exact limits of the dimension.

questions.topic: Meaning, examples and principles of one-point perspective
questions.stem: One-point perspective drawing is commonly used to draw
options: long roads, corridors and room interiors
questions.explanation: Scenes that recede straight away from the viewer suit one-point perspective.

questions.topic: Meaning, examples and principles of one-point perspective
questions.stem: In perspective drawing, objects appear
options: larger as they move further away
smaller as they move further away from the viewer
the same size at any distance
questions.explanation: Things far away look smaller, and perspective drawing shows this.

questions.topic: Meaning, examples and principles of one-point perspective
questions.stem: In perspective drawing, the horizon line represents the
questions.explanation: The horizon line is drawn at the viewer's eye level, and vanishing points are placed on it.

questions.stem: In one-point perspective drawing of a box facing the viewer, the vertical edges are drawn
options: vertical, and the front horizontal edges remain horizontal
questions.explanation: Only the receding lines converge to the vanishing point; verticals stay vertical and front horizontals stay horizontal.

questions.stem: The most suitable tool for measuring the length of a line accurately on a drawing is a
questions.explanation: A rule marked in millimetres measures straight lengths accurately.

questions.stem: A drawing made to the scale 1:1 is called a
questions.explanation: At 1:1 the drawing is the same size as the object.

questions.stem: A line 250 mm long is drawn to a scale of 1:5. What is its length on the drawing?
questions.explanation: At 1:5 the drawing is one-fifth of the real size: 250 / 5 = 50 mm.

questions.stem: A small part 15 mm long is drawn to a scale of 2:1. What is its length on the drawing?
questions.explanation: At 2:1 the drawing is twice the real size: 15 x 2 = 30 mm.

questions.stem: On a building plan drawn to a scale of 1:50, a wall measures 45 mm. What is the actual length of the wall?
questions.explanation: Actual length = 45 x 50 = 2,250 mm = 2.25 m.

questions.topic: Symbols used in plans and blueprints
questions.stem: On a building plan, the letters WC stand for
questions.explanation: WC is the standard abbreviation for a water closet.

questions.topic: Symbols used in plans and blueprints
questions.stem: An arrow marked N on a site plan shows the
questions.explanation: The north point shows how the building is oriented on the site.

questions.topic: Identification of building components on plans
questions.stem: A floor plan of a house shows
options: the front of the house only
the arrangement of rooms as seen from above
questions.explanation: A floor plan is a horizontal section showing rooms, doors and windows from above.

questions.topic: Identification of building components on plans
questions.stem: In a building, the septic tank and soak-away are used for
questions.explanation: Waste from toilets settles and is treated in the septic tank, and liquid drains into the soil through the soak-away.

questions.topic: Identification of building components on plans
questions.stem: Sinks, baths, showers and water closets shown on a building plan are called
questions.explanation: Sanitary wares are the fittings used for washing and disposal of waste water.

questions.stem: A site plan differs from a floor plan because it shows the
options: position of the building on the plot with boundaries and access roads
arrangement of furniture in each room
questions.explanation: The site plan shows the building in relation to the plot boundaries, roads and surroundings.

questions.stem: A claw hammer is used for
options: driving nails and pulling them out
questions.explanation: The face drives nails and the split claw levers them out.

questions.stem: A screwdriver is used to
questions.explanation: The tip of a screwdriver fits the slot of a screw to turn it in or out.

questions.stem: A bradawl is used in woodwork to
options: make small starting holes for screws and nails
questions.explanation: The bradawl's small blade pierces the wood so screws start easily without splitting it.

questions.stem: A bench vice is used to
options: hold work firmly on the bench while it is worked on
questions.explanation: The vice clamps the work so both hands are free to use tools safely.

questions.stem: The saw used for making fine, straight cuts in joints such as tenons is the
questions.explanation: The tenon saw has fine teeth and a stiff back for accurate joint cuts.

questions.stem: A bevel-edged chisel is mainly used for
options: chopping deep mortises with a mallet
paring and cutting into tight corners such as dovetails
questions.explanation: Its bevelled sides let it reach into corners and undercut angles that a firmer chisel cannot.

questions.stem: The tool used to mark and check angles other than 90 degrees on wood is the
questions.explanation: The sliding bevel has an adjustable blade that can be set and locked at any angle.

questions.topic: Care and maintenance of woodwork hand tools
questions.stem: Saws should be stored
options: hung up or in a rack so that the teeth are protected
thrown into a box with hammers
questions.explanation: Proper storage keeps the teeth sharp and prevents accidents.

questions.stem: A surface plate is used in metalwork as a
options: flat reference surface for marking out and testing flatness
questions.explanation: Its accurately flat surface is used with tools such as scribing blocks and squares.

questions.stem: An odd-leg caliper is used to
options: scribe lines parallel to the edge of a workpiece
measure the depth of holes only
questions.explanation: One leg runs along the edge while the other scribes a parallel line.

questions.stem: The engineer's square is used in metalwork to
questions.explanation: It tests whether surfaces and edges are at 90 degrees.

questions.stem: Which instrument measures very small dimensions, such as the diameter of a wire, to about 0.01 mm?
questions.explanation: A micrometer uses a fine screw thread to give very accurate readings.

questions.stem: A cold chisel is used for
questions.explanation: Cold chisels are hardened tools struck with a hammer to cut metal.

questions.topic: Care and maintenance of metalwork tools
questions.stem: When fitting a new blade into a hacksaw frame, the teeth should point
questions.explanation: A hacksaw cuts on the forward stroke, so the teeth must face forward.

questions.stem: Oiling a bicycle chain regularly is an example of
questions.explanation: Regular oiling keeps the chain working smoothly and prevents rust.

questions.stem: Mending the broken leg of a classroom chair after it has failed is an example of
questions.explanation: Corrective maintenance restores equipment after it has broken down.

questions.stem: Checking the vibration and temperature of a machine regularly to forecast when a part will fail is called
questions.explanation: Predictive maintenance uses monitoring to estimate when repairs will be needed.

questions.stem: One importance of maintaining tools and machines is that it
questions.explanation: Well-maintained machines work reliably and safely.

questions.stem: Keeping a log book for a school generator is important because it
options: records services and repairs so the next service can be planned
makes the generator run without fuel
questions.explanation: Records show what has been done and when the next service is due.

questions.topic: Types and uses of woodwork machines
questions.stem: The circular saw is used mainly for
options: ripping and cross-cutting timber in straight lines
questions.explanation: Its round toothed blade makes fast straight cuts.

questions.topic: Types and uses of woodwork machines
questions.stem: The portable electric belt sander is used for
questions.explanation: A moving abrasive belt removes material and smooths the surface.

questions.topic: Types and uses of woodwork machines
questions.stem: A fret saw is used for
options: cutting intricate curves and shapes in thin wood
questions.explanation: Its very fine blade can follow tight curves in thin boards.

questions.stem: The thicknesser is used to
options: reduce boards to a uniform thickness
questions.explanation: Boards fed through the thicknesser come out with an even thickness.

questions.stem: The surface planer is used mainly to
options: plane a flat face and a square edge on rough timber
questions.explanation: The surface planer produces the first flat face and edge, which are then used as references.

questions.topic: Care and maintenance of woodwork machines
questions.stem: Which of the following is good care of woodwork machines?
options: Cleaning the machine while it is running
Keeping blades sharp and removing sawdust after use
Leaving sawdust to build up on the machine
questions.explanation: Sharp blades cut safely, and clean machines do not overheat or jam.

questions.stem: The machine used to make holes in metal is the
questions.explanation: A drilling machine rotates a drill bit to make holes.

questions.stem: The machine that cuts metal bars to length automatically with a reciprocating blade is the
questions.explanation: A power hacksaw moves its blade back and forth by motor, cutting bars and rods.

questions.stem: The shaping machine is used mainly to
options: produce flat surfaces on metal with a single-point tool moving back and forth
questions.explanation: The tool on the ram of the shaper moves in straight strokes over the work, producing flat surfaces.

questions.stem: A machine that removes metal with a rotating cutter having many teeth is the
questions.explanation: Milling cutters have many teeth and produce flat surfaces, slots and gear teeth.

questions.topic: Care and maintenance of metalwork machines
questions.stem: Swarf (metal chips) on a machine should be removed with
options: a brush, after stopping the machine
a wet cloth while it is running
bare hands while the machine is running
questions.explanation: Swarf is sharp and hot, so it is removed with a brush only when the machine has stopped.

questions.topic: Care and maintenance of metalwork machines
questions.stem: A coolant is used during metal cutting on machines mainly to
options: cool and lubricate the cutting tool and work
questions.explanation: Coolant reduces heat and friction, protecting the tool and improving the finish.

questions.topic: Examples of belt and chain drives
questions.stem: A motorcycle usually transmits power from the engine to the rear wheel by a
questions.explanation: A chain and sprockets carry the drive to the rear wheel.

questions.topic: Examples of belt and chain drives
questions.stem: In a local grinding machine (corn mill), the engine usually drives the mill through a
questions.explanation: A belt over pulleys on the engine and the mill transmits the power.

questions.topic: Application of belt and chain drives
questions.stem: A crossed belt drive is used when the
options: driven pulley must turn in the opposite direction to the driver
two pulleys must turn in the same direction
questions.explanation: Crossing the belt makes the driven pulley rotate in the opposite direction.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of belt and chain drives
questions.stem: An advantage of a belt drive is that it
questions.explanation: Belts are cheap and quiet, and their flexibility absorbs sudden loads.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of belt and chain drives
questions.stem: A disadvantage of a chain drive is that it
options: needs regular lubrication and can be noisy
questions.explanation: Chains must be oiled to reduce wear and they make more noise than belts.

questions.topic: Examples of hydraulic and pneumatic devices
questions.stem: Pneumatic devices work by using
questions.explanation: Pneumatic means operated by air under pressure.

questions.topic: Examples of hydraulic and pneumatic devices
questions.stem: Which of the following is a pneumatic device?
options: An air-operated tyre inflator or jackhammer
questions.explanation: Tyre inflators and jackhammers use compressed air.

questions.topic: Components of hydraulic and pneumatic machines
questions.stem: In a hydraulic system, the tank that stores the hydraulic fluid is the
questions.explanation: The reservoir holds the fluid that the pump supplies to the system.

questions.topic: Operation and uses of hydraulic and pneumatic machines
questions.stem: Hydraulic machines use liquids such as oil mainly because liquids
options: cannot easily be compressed, so they transmit force well
questions.explanation: An almost incompressible liquid passes pressure from one piston to another without loss.

questions.topic: Operation and uses of hydraulic and pneumatic machines
questions.stem: In motor cars, hydraulic systems are used in the
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brakes use fluid pressure to push the brake pads against the discs or drums.

questions.stem: Gears are
options: toothed wheels that mesh to transmit motion
questions.explanation: Gear teeth interlock so that one gear drives another.

questions.stem: A gear with its teeth cut on the inside of a ring is called
questions.explanation: Internal gears have teeth inside the rim, and a smaller gear meshes inside them.

questions.stem: Two external gears that mesh directly with each other turn
questions.explanation: The teeth of one push the teeth of the other, so meshing external gears rotate in opposite directions.

questions.stem: An idler gear placed between a driver gear and a driven gear makes the two gears
questions.explanation: The idler reverses direction once more, so the driver and driven turn the same way.

questions.topic: Gear ratios and speed of rotation
questions.stem: A driver gear with 40 teeth turns at 300 revolutions per minute and drives a gear with 20 teeth. At what speed does the driven gear turn?
questions.explanation: Driven speed = driver speed x driver teeth / driven teeth = 300 x 40 / 20 = 600 rev/min.

questions.stem: Grease or oil applied to gears also helps to
options: prevent rusting of the gear teeth
questions.explanation: Lubricants form a protective film that keeps moisture away and prevents rust.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a woodwork project?
options: A dustbin made of sheet metal
questions.explanation: A book rack is made from wood using woodwork tools.

questions.stem: The corners of a wooden photo frame are commonly joined with a
questions.explanation: Mitre joints are cut at 45 degrees so the frame corners look neat.

questions.stem: Before making a wooden stool, the first step is to
options: prepare a working drawing and cutting list
questions.explanation: The drawing and cutting list show the sizes and number of pieces needed.

questions.stem: A cutting list for a woodwork project shows
options: the price of the finished product only
the number, sizes and material of each piece needed
questions.explanation: It allows timber to be bought and cut with little waste.

questions.stem: A coal pot is usually made from
questions.explanation: Coal pots are made by cutting, bending and joining mild steel sheets.

questions.stem: A finished metal stool is painted mainly to
options: prevent rusting and improve its appearance
questions.explanation: Paint keeps air and moisture away from the steel.

questions.stem: The legs of a metal bench are commonly joined to the frame by
questions.explanation: Welding melts and fuses the metal parts to form strong permanent joints.

questions.stem: Joining two metal sheets permanently by passing a metal pin through holes and hammering its end flat is called
questions.explanation: A rivet is closed by hammering, forming a permanent joint.

questions.topic: Soldering and brazing tools and materials
questions.stem: The tool used to heat the joint and melt solder in electrical work is the
questions.explanation: A soldering iron has a heated copper bit that melts the solder.

questions.topic: Soldering and brazing tools and materials
questions.stem: In brazing, the filler metal (spelter) is mainly an alloy of
questions.explanation: Brazing spelter is a brass-type alloy of copper and zinc with a higher melting point than soft solder.

questions.topic: Soldering and brazing operations, types and uses
questions.stem: Soldering is commonly used to join
options: wires and components on electronic circuit boards
questions.explanation: Soft soldering makes good electrical connections at low temperatures.

questions.topic: Soldering and brazing operations, types and uses
questions.stem: Brazing is usually carried out with a
questions.explanation: Brazing needs higher temperatures than soft soldering, so a gas flame is used.

questions.stem: Which of the following shows linear motion?
options: A sliding door moving along its track
questions.explanation: A sliding door moves in a straight line.

questions.stem: In mechanical systems, slides and slots are used to
options: guide a moving part in a straight line
questions.explanation: Slides and slots keep parts such as drawers and lathe carriages moving in straight lines.

questions.stem: A pair of scissors is a first-class lever because the
options: load is between the pivot and the effort
pivot is between the effort and the load
effort is between the pivot and the load
questions.explanation: In a first-class lever the fulcrum lies between effort and load.

questions.stem: A lever lifts a load of 600 N with an effort of 150 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
questions.explanation: Mechanical advantage = load / effort = 600 / 150 = 4.

questions.stem: The blades of a ceiling fan show
questions.explanation: The blades turn in a circle about the central shaft.

questions.stem: A ratchet allows a shaft to rotate
questions.explanation: The pawl drops into the ratchet teeth, stopping motion in the reverse direction.

questions.stem: The load drum of a crane that winds the cable in to lift a load and out to lower it shows
questions.explanation: The drum turns one way to lift and the other way to lower.

questions.topic: Principles of application of rotary motion
questions.stem: A cam and follower is used in engines to change
options: linear motion into rotary motion of the cam
questions.explanation: As the shaped cam rotates, it pushes the follower up and down, for example to open engine valves.

questions.topic: Conversion of rotary motion to linear motion
questions.stem: A screw jack used to lift a car converts
options: rotary motion of the handle into linear (upward) motion
questions.explanation: Turning the screw raises the load in a straight line.

questions.stem:
(a) State four causes of accidents in the school workshop. [4 marks]
(b) Name three workshop safety devices and state the use of each. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Carelessness or playing in the workshop
1 mark: (a) Using blunt or damaged tools
1 mark: (a) Oil or water spilled on the floor
1 mark: (a) Loose clothing, faulty wiring or lack of supervision
1 mark: (b) Goggles
1 mark: (b) Protect the eyes from flying particles
1 mark: (b) Fire extinguisher
1 mark: (b) Put out small fires
1 mark: (b) Any other, e.g. machine guard, safety boots, gloves, first aid box
1 mark: (b) Correct use, e.g. guard keeps hands from moving parts
questions.explanation: Most workshop accidents come from careless behaviour, poor tools and unsafe conditions, and safety devices protect workers from these hazards.

questions.stem:
(a) What is first aid? [2 marks]
(b) List four items found in a first aid box. [4 marks]
(c) Explain what each letter of the ABC of first aid means. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) First aid is the immediate help given to an injured or sick person before professional medical help arrives
1 mark: (b) Sterile bandages or gauze
1 mark: (b) Antiseptic solution or cream
1 mark: (b) Plaster (adhesive dressing) or cotton wool
1 mark: (b) Scissors, gloves or triangular bandage
1 mark: (c) A - Airway: make sure the airway is open and clear
1 mark: (c) B - Breathing: check that the casualty is breathing
1 mark: (c) B also covers bleeding and breaks: stop bleeding and support broken limbs
1 mark: (c) C - Circulation: check the pulse to make sure blood is circulating
questions.explanation: First aid keeps the casualty alive until help arrives; the ABC order deals with the most life-threatening problems first.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the following terms in timber processing: (i) felling (ii) conversion (iii) seasoning. [6 marks]
(b) State two methods of seasoning timber and two reasons for seasoning. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) Felling: cutting down a mature tree
2 marks: (a)(ii) Conversion: sawing logs into planks, boards and other useful sizes
2 marks: (a)(iii) Seasoning: drying timber to reduce its moisture content to a suitable level
1 mark: (b) Air (natural) seasoning
1 mark: (b) Kiln (artificial) seasoning
1 mark: (b) Reason: to make timber stable, reducing shrinking, warping and splitting
1 mark: (b) Reason: to make it lighter, stronger, easier to work and resistant to decay and insects
questions.explanation: Timber goes from tree to usable wood through felling, conversion and seasoning, and seasoning makes it stable and durable.

questions.stem:
(a) What is an alloy? [2 marks]
(b) Give the main components of the following alloys and ONE use of each: (i) brass (ii) bronze (iii) steel. [6 marks]
(c) Name two methods of processing metals. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) An alloy is a mixture of a metal with one or more other metals or elements
1 mark: (b)(i) Brass: copper and zinc
1 mark: (b)(i) Use, e.g. taps, door handles, ornaments
1 mark: (b)(ii) Bronze: copper and tin
1 mark: (b)(ii) Use, e.g. statues, medals, bearings
1 mark: (b)(iii) Steel: iron and carbon
1 mark: (b)(iii) Use, e.g. building rods, tools, car bodies
1 mark: (c) e.g. casting or forging
1 mark: (c) e.g. rolling, drawing or smelting
questions.explanation: Alloys combine metals to improve their properties. Metals are processed by smelting, casting, forging, rolling and drawing.

questions.topic: Uses of drawing instruments and materials
questions.stem: Name five drawing instruments or materials and state ONE use of each. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Tee-square
1 mark: Drawing horizontal lines and guiding set squares
1 mark: Set square (45 or 30/60 degree)
1 mark: Drawing vertical and inclined lines
1 mark: Pair of compasses
1 mark: Drawing circles and arcs
1 mark: Drawing board
1 mark: Supporting the drawing paper
1 mark: Any other, e.g. French curve, protractor, dividers, eraser, scale rule
1 mark: Its correct use
questions.explanation: Each drawing instrument has a special job, and using the right one gives accurate drawings.

questions.stem:
Technical drawing (answer in writing). Triangle ABC has sides AB = 75 mm, BC = 65 mm and AC = 55 mm.
(a) Describe how you would construct the triangle. [4 marks]
(b) Describe how you would construct the circle that passes through A, B and C (circumscribed circle). [6 marks]
(c) What is the centre of this circle called? [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Draw AB = 75 mm
1 mark: (a) With centre A and radius 55 mm, draw an arc
1 mark: (a) With centre B and radius 65 mm, draw an arc to cut the first arc at C
1 mark: (a) Join AC and BC
2 marks: (b) Bisect side AB (arcs from A and B above and below, join the intersections)
2 marks: (b) Bisect a second side, e.g. BC, in the same way
1 mark: (b) Mark O where the perpendicular bisectors meet
1 mark: (b) With centre O and radius OA, draw the circle through A, B and C
2 marks: (c) The circumcentre
questions.explanation: The triangle is built from its three sides using arcs. The point where the perpendicular bisectors of the sides meet is equidistant from A, B and C, so it is the centre of the circumscribed circle.

questions.stem:
Technical drawing (answer in writing). A regular heptagon of side 40 mm is to be constructed by the general method.
(a) How many sides does a heptagon have, and what is each interior angle (to the nearest degree)? [4 marks]
(b) Describe the steps of the general method of constructing the heptagon on a side AB of 40 mm. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Seven sides
1 mark: (a) Sum of interior angles = (7 - 2) x 180 = 900 degrees
2 marks: (a) Each interior angle = 900 / 7, about 129 degrees
1 mark: (b) Draw AB = 40 mm and extend BA beyond A
1 mark: (b) With centre A and radius AB, draw a semicircle
2 marks: (b) Divide the semicircle into seven equal parts (by protractor or trial) and number the divisions
1 mark: (b) Join A to division 2; this gives the second side
1 mark: (b) Draw radial lines from A through the remaining divisions
1 mark: (b) Step off 40 mm along each line (or use arcs of radius AB from each new corner) to locate the other corners
1 mark: (b) Join the corners to complete the heptagon
questions.explanation: The general method divides a semicircle on one side into as many parts as the polygon has sides; the line to division 2 gives the angle for the second side.

questions.stem:
Technical drawing (answer in writing). A rectangle measures 90 mm by 40 mm.
(a) Calculate the area of the rectangle. [2 marks]
(b) Calculate the side of a square of equal area. [2 marks]
(c) Describe a geometrical construction of a square equal in area to the rectangle (mean proportional method). [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Area = 90 x 40 = 3,600 square millimetres
2 marks: (b) Side = square root of 3,600 = 60 mm
1 mark: (c) Draw the long side AB = 90 mm and extend it by the short side (40 mm) to C, so AC = 130 mm
1 mark: (c) Bisect AC to find its midpoint O
1 mark: (c) With centre O and radius OA, draw a semicircle on AC
1 mark: (c) At B, draw a perpendicular to cut the semicircle at D
1 mark: (c) BD is the side of the required square (it measures 60 mm)
1 mark: (c) Complete the square on BD
questions.explanation: The side of the equal square is the mean proportional of the rectangle's sides, found with a semicircle; it can be checked by calculation as 60 mm.

questions.topic: Placing principal views in the quadrants
questions.stem:
(a) Name the three principal views used in orthographic projection. [3 marks]
(b) In first angle projection, state where the plan and the end view seen from the left are placed in relation to the front elevation. [4 marks]
(c) State three types of lines used in orthographic drawings and what each shows. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Front elevation
1 mark: (a) End (side) elevation
1 mark: (a) Plan
2 marks: (b) The plan is placed directly below the front elevation
2 marks: (b) The view from the left is placed to the right of the front elevation
1 mark: (c) Thick continuous lines: visible outlines
1 mark: (c) Short dashes: hidden details
1 mark: (c) Chain lines: centre lines (accept thin lines for dimension and projection lines)
questions.explanation: In first angle projection each view is placed on the side opposite the direction of viewing. Different line types show outlines, hidden detail and centres.

questions.topic: Isometric drawing of simple shape blocks
questions.stem:
(a) State three differences between isometric and oblique drawing. [6 marks]
(b) Describe how you would start an isometric drawing of a rectangular block 80 mm long, 50 mm wide and 40 mm high. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Isometric: receding lines at 30 degrees on both sides; oblique: front face drawn flat with receding lines usually at 45 degrees
2 marks: (a) Isometric shows no face in its true shape; oblique shows the front face in its true shape
2 marks: (a) Isometric uses true lengths on all three axes; cabinet oblique halves the receding depth
1 mark: (b) Draw a vertical line 40 mm for the front corner
1 mark: (b) From the bottom of this line, draw lines at 30 degrees to left and right using the tee-square and 30/60 set square
1 mark: (b) Mark 80 mm along one 30-degree line and 50 mm along the other
1 mark: (b) Draw verticals and parallel lines to complete the block
questions.explanation: Isometric drawing uses three axes 120 degrees apart; oblique drawing keeps the front face true and adds receding lines.

questions.stem:
(a) What is a scale drawing? [2 marks]
(b) State the meaning of each of these scales: (i) 1:1 (ii) 1:20 (iii) 2:1. [3 marks]
(c) A room 4.5 m long and 3 m wide is drawn to a scale of 1:50. Calculate its length and width on the drawing. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) A drawing in which an object is drawn larger, smaller or the same size as the real object in a fixed ratio
1 mark: (b)(i) Full size
1 mark: (b)(ii) Reduction: the drawing is one-twentieth of the actual size
1 mark: (b)(iii) Enlargement: the drawing is twice the actual size
1 mark: (c) Convert to millimetres: 4,500 mm and 3,000 mm
2 marks: (c) Length = 4,500 / 50 = 90 mm
2 marks: (c) Width = 3,000 / 50 = 60 mm
questions.explanation: Scales show the ratio between drawing size and real size. Dividing real sizes by 50 gives the drawing sizes.

questions.topic: Gear ratios and speed of rotation
questions.stem:
A driver gear A with 24 teeth meshes with a driven gear B with 72 teeth. Gear A turns at 600 rev/min.
(a) Calculate the gear ratio. [3 marks]
(b) Calculate the speed of gear B. [4 marks]
(c) State the direction of rotation of B compared with A, and what could be added to make them turn the same way. [3 marks]
(d) State two functions of lubricants in gears. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Gear ratio = teeth on driven / teeth on driver
2 marks: (a) = 72 / 24 = 3:1
1 mark: (b) Speed of B = speed of A x teeth on A / teeth on B
1 mark: (b) = 600 x 24 / 72
2 marks: (b) = 200 rev/min
2 marks: (c) B turns in the opposite direction to A
1 mark: (c) An idler gear placed between them
1 mark: (d) Reduce friction and wear
1 mark: (d) Cool the gears / prevent rust / reduce noise
questions.explanation: A larger driven gear turns more slowly. Meshing external gears reverse direction, which an idler gear corrects.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of belt and chain drives
questions.stem:
(a) Give two examples each of machines that use belt drives and chain drives. [4 marks]
(b) State two advantages and one disadvantage of a belt drive. [3 marks]
(c) State two advantages and one disadvantage of a chain drive. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Belt: car engine fan belt
1 mark: (a) Belt: grinding mill, sewing machine or washing machine
1 mark: (a) Chain: bicycle
1 mark: (a) Chain: motorcycle or conveyor
1 mark: (b) Advantage: quiet and cheap
1 mark: (b) Advantage: absorbs shock and needs no lubrication
1 mark: (b) Disadvantage: may slip under heavy load / stretches and wears
1 mark: (c) Advantage: does not slip, so it gives a fixed speed ratio
1 mark: (c) Advantage: transmits heavy loads and is strong
1 mark: (c) Disadvantage: needs lubrication / noisy / heavier and more costly
questions.explanation: Belts are quiet and cheap but may slip; chains are positive and strong but need oiling.

questions.topic: Conversion of rotary motion to linear motion
questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between linear motion and rotary motion, giving ONE example of each. [4 marks]
(b) Name four mechanisms that convert rotary motion to linear motion or linear to rotary motion, and give ONE example of where each is used. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Linear motion is movement in a straight line
1 mark: (a) e.g. a sliding drawer, a lift, a train on a straight track
1 mark: (a) Rotary motion is movement in a circle about an axis
1 mark: (a) e.g. a wheel, a ceiling fan
1 mark: (b) Rack and pinion
1 mark: (b) e.g. car steering or a pillar drill feed
1 mark: (b) Screw (lead screw / screw jack)
1 mark: (b) e.g. car jack, vice or lathe carriage
1 mark: (b) Crank and slider / connecting rod and piston
1 mark: (b) e.g. car engine or pump
1 mark: (b) Cam and follower
1 mark: (b) e.g. engine valve operation
questions.explanation: Machines often need to change rotary motion into straight-line motion or the reverse, using mechanisms such as rack and pinion, screws, cranks and cams.
